An owner of residential rental property or their agent charging an application screening fee must limit it to actual out-of-pocket information-gathering costs plus the reasonable value of time spent obtaining applicant information. The fee also must not exceed $30 per applicant, subject to annual adjustments commensurate with increases in the Consumer Price Index beginning January 1, 1998. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available then or will be available within a reasonable period. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent may collect an application screening fee only if, at collection, they offer either the ordered-consideration process with written criteria, first-qualified approval and consideration-linked charging, or the process refunding every unselected applicant's entire fee. The first process requires correction of qualifying inadvertent charges within seven days, subject to the applicant's discretionary alternative credit, while the second requires refunds by the earlier of seven days after selecting a tenant or 30 days after application submission. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant a receipt for a paid application screening fee, itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent obtaining and processing applicant information. Delivery must be personal or by mail, with a copy to an applicant-provided email account permitted by agreement between the landlord or agent and applicant. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an owner of residential rental property or their agent does not perform a personal reference check or does not obtain a consumer credit report, they must return to the applicant any screening fee amount not used for purposes authorized by this section. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an applicant has paid an application screening fee, the owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant who is the report's subject a copy of the consumer credit report by personal delivery, mail or email within seven days after receiving it. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

A0275.explanation: A person, as defined by Section 16702 and excluding an end consumer, must not use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, trust combination, or conspiracy restraining trade or commerce in violation of the Cartwright Act. This prohibition concerns methodologies used by two or more persons that use competitor data to influence a price or commercial term.

A person, as defined by Section 16702 and excluding an end consumer, must not use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if that person coerces another person to set or adopt its recommended price or commercial term for the same or similar products or services in California. This prohibition concerns methodologies used by two or more persons that use competitor data to influence a price or commercial term.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent charging an application screening fee must limit it to actual out-of-pocket information-gathering costs plus the reasonable value of time spent obtaining applicant information. The fee also must not exceed $30 per applicant, subject to annual adjustments commensurate with increases in the Consumer Price Index beginning January 1, 1998. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 15 Units or more”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available then or will be available within a reasonable period. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 15 Units or more”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent may collect an application screening fee only if, at collection, they offer either the ordered-consideration process with written criteria, first-qualified approval and consideration-linked charging, or the process refunding every unselected applicant's entire fee. The first process requires correction of qualifying inadvertent charges within seven days, subject to the applicant's discretionary alternative credit, while the second requires refunds by the earlier of seven days after selecting a tenant or 30 days after application submission. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 15 Units or more”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant a receipt for a paid application screening fee, itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent obtaining and processing applicant information. Delivery must be personal or by mail, with a copy to an applicant-provided email account permitted by agreement between the landlord or agent and applicant. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 15 Units or more”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an owner of residential rental property or their agent does not perform a personal reference check or does not obtain a consumer credit report, they must return to the applicant any screening fee amount not used for purposes authorized by this section. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 15 Units or more”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an applicant has paid an application screening fee, the owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant who is the report's subject a copy of the consumer credit report by personal delivery, mail or email within seven days after receiving it. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 15 Units or more”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent charging an application screening fee must limit it to actual out-of-pocket information-gathering costs plus the reasonable value of time spent obtaining applicant information. The fee also must not exceed $30 per applicant, subject to annual adjustments commensurate with increases in the Consumer Price Index beginning January 1, 1998. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available then or will be available within a reasonable period. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent may collect an application screening fee only if, at collection, they offer either the ordered-consideration process with written criteria, first-qualified approval and consideration-linked charging, or the process refunding every unselected applicant's entire fee. The first process requires correction of qualifying inadvertent charges within seven days, subject to the applicant's discretionary alternative credit, while the second requires refunds by the earlier of seven days after selecting a tenant or 30 days after application submission. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant a receipt for a paid application screening fee, itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent obtaining and processing applicant information. Delivery must be personal or by mail, with a copy to an applicant-provided email account permitted by agreement between the landlord or agent and applicant. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an owner of residential rental property or their agent does not perform a personal reference check or does not obtain a consumer credit report, they must return to the applicant any screening fee amount not used for purposes authorized by this section. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an applicant has paid an application screening fee, the owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant who is the report's subject a copy of the consumer credit report by personal delivery, mail or email within seven days after receiving it. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent charging an application screening fee must limit it to actual out-of-pocket information-gathering costs plus the reasonable value of time spent obtaining applicant information. The fee also must not exceed $30 per applicant, subject to annual adjustments commensurate with increases in the Consumer Price Index beginning January 1, 1998. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available then or will be available within a reasonable period. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent may collect an application screening fee only if, at collection, they offer either the ordered-consideration process with written criteria, first-qualified approval and consideration-linked charging, or the process refunding every unselected applicant's entire fee. The first process requires correction of qualifying inadvertent charges within seven days, subject to the applicant's discretionary alternative credit, while the second requires refunds by the earlier of seven days after selecting a tenant or 30 days after application submission. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant a receipt for a paid application screening fee, itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent obtaining and processing applicant information. Delivery must be personal or by mail, with a copy to an applicant-provided email account permitted by agreement between the landlord or agent and applicant. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an owner of residential rental property or their agent does not perform a personal reference check or does not obtain a consumer credit report, they must return to the applicant any screening fee amount not used for purposes authorized by this section. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an applicant has paid an application screening fee, the owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant who is the report's subject a copy of the consumer credit report by personal delivery, mail or email within seven days after receiving it. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent charging an application screening fee must limit it to actual out-of-pocket information-gathering costs plus the reasonable value of time spent obtaining applicant information. The fee also must not exceed $30 per applicant, subject to annual adjustments commensurate with increases in the Consumer Price Index beginning January 1, 1998. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available then or will be available within a reasonable period. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent may collect an application screening fee only if, at collection, they offer either the ordered-consideration process with written criteria, first-qualified approval and consideration-linked charging, or the process refunding every unselected applicant's entire fee. The first process requires correction of qualifying inadvertent charges within seven days, subject to the applicant's discretionary alternative credit, while the second requires refunds by the earlier of seven days after selecting a tenant or 30 days after application submission. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant a receipt for a paid application screening fee, itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent obtaining and processing applicant information. Delivery must be personal or by mail, with a copy to an applicant-provided email account permitted by agreement between the landlord or agent and applicant. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an owner of residential rental property or their agent does not perform a personal reference check or does not obtain a consumer credit report, they must return to the applicant any screening fee amount not used for purposes authorized by this section. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an applicant has paid an application screening fee, the owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant who is the report's subject a copy of the consumer credit report by personal delivery, mail or email within seven days after receiving it. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent charging an application screening fee must limit it to actual out-of-pocket information-gathering costs plus the reasonable value of time spent obtaining applicant information. The fee also must not exceed $30 per applicant, subject to annual adjustments commensurate with increases in the Consumer Price Index beginning January 1, 1998. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available then or will be available within a reasonable period. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent may collect an application screening fee only if, at collection, they offer either the ordered-consideration process with written criteria, first-qualified approval and consideration-linked charging, or the process refunding every unselected applicant's entire fee. The first process requires correction of qualifying inadvertent charges within seven days, subject to the applicant's discretionary alternative credit, while the second requires refunds by the earlier of seven days after selecting a tenant or 30 days after application submission. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant a receipt for a paid application screening fee, itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent obtaining and processing applicant information. Delivery must be personal or by mail, with a copy to an applicant-provided email account permitted by agreement between the landlord or agent and applicant. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an owner of residential rental property or their agent does not perform a personal reference check or does not obtain a consumer credit report, they must return to the applicant any screening fee amount not used for purposes authorized by this section. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an applicant has paid an application screening fee, the owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant who is the report's subject a copy of the consumer credit report by personal delivery, mail or email within seven days after receiving it. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent charging an application screening fee must limit it to actual out-of-pocket information-gathering costs plus the reasonable value of time spent obtaining applicant information. The fee also must not exceed $30 per applicant, subject to annual adjustments commensurate with increases in the Consumer Price Index beginning January 1, 1998. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available then or will be available within a reasonable period. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent may collect an application screening fee only if, at collection, they offer either the ordered-consideration process with written criteria, first-qualified approval and consideration-linked charging, or the process refunding every unselected applicant's entire fee. The first process requires correction of qualifying inadvertent charges within seven days, subject to the applicant's discretionary alternative credit, while the second requires refunds by the earlier of seven days after selecting a tenant or 30 days after application submission. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant a receipt for a paid application screening fee, itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent obtaining and processing applicant information. Delivery must be personal or by mail, with a copy to an applicant-provided email account permitted by agreement between the landlord or agent and applicant. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an owner of residential rental property or their agent does not perform a personal reference check or does not obtain a consumer credit report, they must return to the applicant any screening fee amount not used for purposes authorized by this section. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an applicant has paid an application screening fee, the owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant who is the report's subject a copy of the consumer credit report by personal delivery, mail or email within seven days after receiving it. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent charging an application screening fee must limit it to actual out-of-pocket information-gathering costs plus the reasonable value of time spent obtaining applicant information. The fee also must not exceed $30 per applicant, subject to annual adjustments commensurate with increases in the Consumer Price Index beginning January 1, 1998. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available then or will be available within a reasonable period. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent may collect an application screening fee only if, at collection, they offer either the ordered-consideration process with written criteria, first-qualified approval and consideration-linked charging, or the process refunding every unselected applicant's entire fee. The first process requires correction of qualifying inadvertent charges within seven days, subject to the applicant's discretionary alternative credit, while the second requires refunds by the earlier of seven days after selecting a tenant or 30 days after application submission. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant a receipt for a paid application screening fee, itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent obtaining and processing applicant information. Delivery must be personal or by mail, with a copy to an applicant-provided email account permitted by agreement between the landlord or agent and applicant. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an owner of residential rental property or their agent does not perform a personal reference check or does not obtain a consumer credit report, they must return to the applicant any screening fee amount not used for purposes authorized by this section. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an applicant has paid an application screening fee, the owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant who is the report's subject a copy of the consumer credit report by personal delivery, mail or email within seven days after receiving it. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent charging an application screening fee must limit it to actual out-of-pocket information-gathering costs plus the reasonable value of time spent obtaining applicant information. The fee also must not exceed $30 per applicant, subject to annual adjustments commensurate with increases in the Consumer Price Index beginning January 1, 1998. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available then or will be available within a reasonable period. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent may collect an application screening fee only if, at collection, they offer either the ordered-consideration process with written criteria, first-qualified approval and consideration-linked charging, or the process refunding every unselected applicant's entire fee. The first process requires correction of qualifying inadvertent charges within seven days, subject to the applicant's discretionary alternative credit, while the second requires refunds by the earlier of seven days after selecting a tenant or 30 days after application submission. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant a receipt for a paid application screening fee, itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent obtaining and processing applicant information. Delivery must be personal or by mail, with a copy to an applicant-provided email account permitted by agreement between the landlord or agent and applicant. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an owner of residential rental property or their agent does not perform a personal reference check or does not obtain a consumer credit report, they must return to the applicant any screening fee amount not used for purposes authorized by this section. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an applicant has paid an application screening fee, the owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant who is the report's subject a copy of the consumer credit report by personal delivery, mail or email within seven days after receiving it. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent charging an application screening fee must limit it to actual out-of-pocket information-gathering costs plus the reasonable value of time spent obtaining applicant information. The fee also must not exceed $30 per applicant, subject to annual adjustments commensurate with increases in the Consumer Price Index beginning January 1, 1998. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available then or will be available within a reasonable period. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent may collect an application screening fee only if, at collection, they offer either the ordered-consideration process with written criteria, first-qualified approval and consideration-linked charging, or the process refunding every unselected applicant's entire fee. The first process requires correction of qualifying inadvertent charges within seven days, subject to the applicant's discretionary alternative credit, while the second requires refunds by the earlier of seven days after selecting a tenant or 30 days after application submission. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant a receipt for a paid application screening fee, itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent obtaining and processing applicant information. Delivery must be personal or by mail, with a copy to an applicant-provided email account permitted by agreement between the landlord or agent and applicant. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an owner of residential rental property or their agent does not perform a personal reference check or does not obtain a consumer credit report, they must return to the applicant any screening fee amount not used for purposes authorized by this section. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an applicant has paid an application screening fee, the owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant who is the report's subject a copy of the consumer credit report by personal delivery, mail or email within seven days after receiving it. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent charging an application screening fee must limit it to actual out-of-pocket information-gathering costs plus the reasonable value of time spent obtaining applicant information. The fee also must not exceed $30 per applicant, subject to annual adjustments commensurate with increases in the Consumer Price Index beginning January 1, 1998. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available then or will be available within a reasonable period. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent may collect an application screening fee only if, at collection, they offer either the ordered-consideration process with written criteria, first-qualified approval and consideration-linked charging, or the process refunding every unselected applicant's entire fee. The first process requires correction of qualifying inadvertent charges within seven days, subject to the applicant's discretionary alternative credit, while the second requires refunds by the earlier of seven days after selecting a tenant or 30 days after application submission. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent charging an application screening fee must limit it to actual out-of-pocket information-gathering costs plus the reasonable value of time spent obtaining applicant information. The fee also must not exceed $30 per applicant, subject to annual adjustments commensurate with increases in the Consumer Price Index beginning January 1, 1998. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available then or will be available within a reasonable period. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent may collect an application screening fee only if, at collection, they offer either the ordered-consideration process with written criteria, first-qualified approval and consideration-linked charging, or the process refunding every unselected applicant's entire fee. The first process requires correction of qualifying inadvertent charges within seven days, subject to the applicant's discretionary alternative credit, while the second requires refunds by the earlier of seven days after selecting a tenant or 30 days after application submission. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant a receipt for a paid application screening fee, itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent obtaining and processing applicant information. Delivery must be personal or by mail, with a copy to an applicant-provided email account permitted by agreement between the landlord or agent and applicant. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an owner of residential rental property or their agent does not perform a personal reference check or does not obtain a consumer credit report, they must return to the applicant any screening fee amount not used for purposes authorized by this section. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an applicant has paid an application screening fee, the owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant who is the report's subject a copy of the consumer credit report by personal delivery, mail or email within seven days after receiving it. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent charging an application screening fee must limit it to actual out-of-pocket information-gathering costs plus the reasonable value of time spent obtaining applicant information. The fee also must not exceed $30 per applicant, subject to annual adjustments commensurate with increases in the Consumer Price Index beginning January 1, 1998. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available then or will be available within a reasonable period. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent may collect an application screening fee only if, at collection, they offer either the ordered-consideration process with written criteria, first-qualified approval and consideration-linked charging, or the process refunding every unselected applicant's entire fee. The first process requires correction of qualifying inadvertent charges within seven days, subject to the applicant's discretionary alternative credit, while the second requires refunds by the earlier of seven days after selecting a tenant or 30 days after application submission. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant a receipt for a paid application screening fee, itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent obtaining and processing applicant information. Delivery must be personal or by mail, with a copy to an applicant-provided email account permitted by agreement between the landlord or agent and applicant. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an owner of residential rental property or their agent does not perform a personal reference check or does not obtain a consumer credit report, they must return to the applicant any screening fee amount not used for purposes authorized by this section. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an applicant has paid an application screening fee, the owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant who is the report's subject a copy of the consumer credit report by personal delivery, mail or email within seven days after receiving it. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent charging an application screening fee must limit it to actual out-of-pocket information-gathering costs plus the reasonable value of time spent obtaining applicant information. The fee also must not exceed $30 per applicant, subject to annual adjustments commensurate with increases in the Consumer Price Index beginning January 1, 1998. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available then or will be available within a reasonable period. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent may collect an application screening fee only if, at collection, they offer either the ordered-consideration process with written criteria, first-qualified approval and consideration-linked charging, or the process refunding every unselected applicant's entire fee. The first process requires correction of qualifying inadvertent charges within seven days, subject to the applicant's discretionary alternative credit, while the second requires refunds by the earlier of seven days after selecting a tenant or 30 days after application submission. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant a receipt for a paid application screening fee, itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent obtaining and processing applicant information. Delivery must be personal or by mail, with a copy to an applicant-provided email account permitted by agreement between the landlord or agent and applicant. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an owner of residential rental property or their agent does not perform a personal reference check or does not obtain a consumer credit report, they must return to the applicant any screening fee amount not used for purposes authorized by this section. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an applicant has paid an application screening fee, the owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant who is the report's subject a copy of the consumer credit report by personal delivery, mail or email within seven days after receiving it. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent charging an application screening fee must limit it to actual out-of-pocket information-gathering costs plus the reasonable value of time spent obtaining applicant information. The fee also must not exceed $30 per applicant, subject to annual adjustments commensurate with increases in the Consumer Price Index beginning January 1, 1998. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available then or will be available within a reasonable period. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent may collect an application screening fee only if, at collection, they offer either the ordered-consideration process with written criteria, first-qualified approval and consideration-linked charging, or the process refunding every unselected applicant's entire fee. The first process requires correction of qualifying inadvertent charges within seven days, subject to the applicant's discretionary alternative credit, while the second requires refunds by the earlier of seven days after selecting a tenant or 30 days after application submission. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant a receipt for a paid application screening fee, itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent obtaining and processing applicant information. Delivery must be personal or by mail, with a copy to an applicant-provided email account permitted by agreement between the landlord or agent and applicant. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an owner of residential rental property or their agent does not perform a personal reference check or does not obtain a consumer credit report, they must return to the applicant any screening fee amount not used for purposes authorized by this section. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an applicant has paid an application screening fee, the owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant who is the report's subject a copy of the consumer credit report by personal delivery, mail or email within seven days after receiving it. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent charging an application screening fee must limit it to actual out-of-pocket information-gathering costs plus the reasonable value of time spent obtaining applicant information. The fee also must not exceed $30 per applicant, subject to annual adjustments commensurate with increases in the Consumer Price Index beginning January 1, 1998. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available then or will be available within a reasonable period. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent may collect an application screening fee only if, at collection, they offer either the ordered-consideration process with written criteria, first-qualified approval and consideration-linked charging, or the process refunding every unselected applicant's entire fee. The first process requires correction of qualifying inadvertent charges within seven days, subject to the applicant's discretionary alternative credit, while the second requires refunds by the earlier of seven days after selecting a tenant or 30 days after application submission. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant a receipt for a paid application screening fee, itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent obtaining and processing applicant information. Delivery must be personal or by mail, with a copy to an applicant-provided email account permitted by agreement between the landlord or agent and applicant. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an owner of residential rental property or their agent does not perform a personal reference check or does not obtain a consumer credit report, they must return to the applicant any screening fee amount not used for purposes authorized by this section. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an applicant has paid an application screening fee, the owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant who is the report's subject a copy of the consumer credit report by personal delivery, mail or email within seven days after receiving it. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent charging an application screening fee must limit it to actual out-of-pocket information-gathering costs plus the reasonable value of time spent obtaining applicant information. The fee also must not exceed $30 per applicant, subject to annual adjustments commensurate with increases in the Consumer Price Index beginning January 1, 1998. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available then or will be available within a reasonable period. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent may collect an application screening fee only if, at collection, they offer either the ordered-consideration process with written criteria, first-qualified approval and consideration-linked charging, or the process refunding every unselected applicant's entire fee. The first process requires correction of qualifying inadvertent charges within seven days, subject to the applicant's discretionary alternative credit, while the second requires refunds by the earlier of seven days after selecting a tenant or 30 days after application submission. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant a receipt for a paid application screening fee, itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent obtaining and processing applicant information. Delivery must be personal or by mail, with a copy to an applicant-provided email account permitted by agreement between the landlord or agent and applicant. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an owner of residential rental property or their agent does not perform a personal reference check or does not obtain a consumer credit report, they must return to the applicant any screening fee amount not used for purposes authorized by this section. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an applicant has paid an application screening fee, the owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant who is the report's subject a copy of the consumer credit report by personal delivery, mail or email within seven days after receiving it. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

A person, as defined by Section 16702 and excluding an end consumer, must not use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if that person coerces another person to set or adopt its recommended price or commercial term for the same or similar products or services in California. This prohibition concerns methodologies used by two or more persons that use competitor data to influence a price or commercial term.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent charging an application screening fee must limit it to actual out-of-pocket information-gathering costs plus the reasonable value of time spent obtaining applicant information. The fee also must not exceed $30 per applicant, subject to annual adjustments commensurate with increases in the Consumer Price Index beginning January 1, 1998. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available then or will be available within a reasonable period. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent may collect an application screening fee only if, at collection, they offer either the ordered-consideration process with written criteria, first-qualified approval and consideration-linked charging, or the process refunding every unselected applicant's entire fee. The first process requires correction of qualifying inadvertent charges within seven days, subject to the applicant's discretionary alternative credit, while the second requires refunds by the earlier of seven days after selecting a tenant or 30 days after application submission. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant a receipt for a paid application screening fee, itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent obtaining and processing applicant information. Delivery must be personal or by mail, with a copy to an applicant-provided email account permitted by agreement between the landlord or agent and applicant. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an owner of residential rental property or their agent does not perform a personal reference check or does not obtain a consumer credit report, they must return to the applicant any screening fee amount not used for purposes authorized by this section. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an applicant has paid an application screening fee, the owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant who is the report's subject a copy of the consumer credit report by personal delivery, mail or email within seven days after receiving it. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent charging an application screening fee must limit it to actual out-of-pocket information-gathering costs plus the reasonable value of time spent obtaining applicant information. The fee also must not exceed $30 per applicant, subject to annual adjustments commensurate with increases in the Consumer Price Index beginning January 1, 1998. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available then or will be available within a reasonable period. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent may collect an application screening fee only if, at collection, they offer either the ordered-consideration process with written criteria, first-qualified approval and consideration-linked charging, or the process refunding every unselected applicant's entire fee. The first process requires correction of qualifying inadvertent charges within seven days, subject to the applicant's discretionary alternative credit, while the second requires refunds by the earlier of seven days after selecting a tenant or 30 days after application submission. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant a receipt for a paid application screening fee, itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent obtaining and processing applicant information. Delivery must be personal or by mail, with a copy to an applicant-provided email account permitted by agreement between the landlord or agent and applicant. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an owner of residential rental property or their agent does not perform a personal reference check or does not obtain a consumer credit report, they must return to the applicant any screening fee amount not used for purposes authorized by this section. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an applicant has paid an application screening fee, the owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant who is the report's subject a copy of the consumer credit report by personal delivery, mail or email within seven days after receiving it. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent charging an application screening fee must limit it to actual out-of-pocket information-gathering costs plus the reasonable value of time spent obtaining applicant information. The fee also must not exceed $30 per applicant, subject to annual adjustments commensurate with increases in the Consumer Price Index beginning January 1, 1998. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available then or will be available within a reasonable period. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent may collect an application screening fee only if, at collection, they offer either the ordered-consideration process with written criteria, first-qualified approval and consideration-linked charging, or the process refunding every unselected applicant's entire fee. The first process requires correction of qualifying inadvertent charges within seven days, subject to the applicant's discretionary alternative credit, while the second requires refunds by the earlier of seven days after selecting a tenant or 30 days after application submission. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant a receipt for a paid application screening fee, itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent obtaining and processing applicant information. Delivery must be personal or by mail, with a copy to an applicant-provided email account permitted by agreement between the landlord or agent and applicant. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an owner of residential rental property or their agent does not perform a personal reference check or does not obtain a consumer credit report, they must return to the applicant any screening fee amount not used for purposes authorized by this section. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an applicant has paid an application screening fee, the owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant who is the report's subject a copy of the consumer credit report by personal delivery, mail or email within seven days after receiving it. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

A0378.explanation: A person, as defined by Section 16702 and excluding an end consumer, must not use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, trust combination, or conspiracy restraining trade or commerce in violation of the Cartwright Act. This prohibition concerns methodologies used by two or more persons that use competitor data to influence a price or commercial term.

A person, as defined by Section 16702 and excluding an end consumer, must not use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if that person coerces another person to set or adopt its recommended price or commercial term for the same or similar products or services in California. This prohibition concerns methodologies used by two or more persons that use competitor data to influence a price or commercial term.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent charging an application screening fee must limit it to actual out-of-pocket information-gathering costs plus the reasonable value of time spent obtaining applicant information. The fee also must not exceed $30 per applicant, subject to annual adjustments commensurate with increases in the Consumer Price Index beginning January 1, 1998. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available then or will be available within a reasonable period. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent may collect an application screening fee only if, at collection, they offer either the ordered-consideration process with written criteria, first-qualified approval and consideration-linked charging, or the process refunding every unselected applicant's entire fee. The first process requires correction of qualifying inadvertent charges within seven days, subject to the applicant's discretionary alternative credit, while the second requires refunds by the earlier of seven days after selecting a tenant or 30 days after application submission. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant a receipt for a paid application screening fee, itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent obtaining and processing applicant information. Delivery must be personal or by mail, with a copy to an applicant-provided email account permitted by agreement between the landlord or agent and applicant. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an owner of residential rental property or their agent does not perform a personal reference check or does not obtain a consumer credit report, they must return to the applicant any screening fee amount not used for purposes authorized by this section. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an applicant has paid an application screening fee, the owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant who is the report's subject a copy of the consumer credit report by personal delivery, mail or email within seven days after receiving it. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

This prohibition concerns methodologies used by two or more persons that use competitor data to influence a price or commercial term.

This prohibition concerns methodologies used by two or more persons that use competitor data to influence a price or commercial term.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent charging an application screening fee must limit it to actual out-of-pocket information-gathering costs plus the reasonable value of time spent obtaining applicant information. The fee also must not exceed $30 per applicant, subject to annual adjustments commensurate with increases in the Consumer Price Index beginning January 1, 1998. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 15 Units or more”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available then or will be available within a reasonable period. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 15 Units or more”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent may collect an application screening fee only if, at collection, they offer either the ordered-consideration process with written criteria, first-qualified approval and consideration-linked charging, or the process refunding every unselected applicant's entire fee. The first process requires correction of qualifying inadvertent charges within seven days, subject to the applicant's discretionary alternative credit, while the second requires refunds by the earlier of seven days after selecting a tenant or 30 days after application submission. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 15 Units or more”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant a receipt for a paid application screening fee, itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent obtaining and processing applicant information. Delivery must be personal or by mail, with a copy to an applicant-provided email account permitted by agreement between the landlord or agent and applicant. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 15 Units or more”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an owner of residential rental property or their agent does not perform a personal reference check or does not obtain a consumer credit report, they must return to the applicant any screening fee amount not used for purposes authorized by this section. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 15 Units or more”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an applicant has paid an application screening fee, the owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant who is the report's subject a copy of the consumer credit report by personal delivery, mail or email within seven days after receiving it. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 15 Units or more”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent charging an application screening fee must limit it to actual out-of-pocket information-gathering costs plus the reasonable value of time spent obtaining applicant information. The fee also must not exceed $30 per applicant, subject to annual adjustments commensurate with increases in the Consumer Price Index beginning January 1, 1998. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available then or will be available within a reasonable period. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent may collect an application screening fee only if, at collection, they offer either the ordered-consideration process with written criteria, first-qualified approval and consideration-linked charging, or the process refunding every unselected applicant's entire fee. The first process requires correction of qualifying inadvertent charges within seven days, subject to the applicant's discretionary alternative credit, while the second requires refunds by the earlier of seven days after selecting a tenant or 30 days after application submission. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent charging an application screening fee must limit it to actual out-of-pocket information-gathering costs plus the reasonable value of time spent obtaining applicant information. The fee also must not exceed $30 per applicant, subject to annual adjustments commensurate with increases in the Consumer Price Index beginning January 1, 1998. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available then or will be available within a reasonable period. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent may collect an application screening fee only if, at collection, they offer either the ordered-consideration process with written criteria, first-qualified approval and consideration-linked charging, or the process refunding every unselected applicant's entire fee. The first process requires correction of qualifying inadvertent charges within seven days, subject to the applicant's discretionary alternative credit, while the second requires refunds by the earlier of seven days after selecting a tenant or 30 days after application submission. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant a receipt for a paid application screening fee, itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent obtaining and processing applicant information. Delivery must be personal or by mail, with a copy to an applicant-provided email account permitted by agreement between the landlord or agent and applicant. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an owner of residential rental property or their agent does not perform a personal reference check or does not obtain a consumer credit report, they must return to the applicant any screening fee amount not used for purposes authorized by this section. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an applicant has paid an application screening fee, the owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant who is the report's subject a copy of the consumer credit report by personal delivery, mail or email within seven days after receiving it. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Five or more apartments”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

This prohibition concerns methodologies used by two or more persons that use competitor data to influence a price or commercial term.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent charging an application screening fee must limit it to actual out-of-pocket information-gathering costs plus the reasonable value of time spent obtaining applicant information. The fee also must not exceed $30 per applicant, subject to annual adjustments commensurate with increases in the Consumer Price Index beginning January 1, 1998. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available then or will be available within a reasonable period. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent may collect an application screening fee only if, at collection, they offer either the ordered-consideration process with written criteria, first-qualified approval and consideration-linked charging, or the process refunding every unselected applicant's entire fee. The first process requires correction of qualifying inadvertent charges within seven days, subject to the applicant's discretionary alternative credit, while the second requires refunds by the earlier of seven days after selecting a tenant or 30 days after application submission. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

An owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant a receipt for a paid application screening fee, itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent obtaining and processing applicant information. Delivery must be personal or by mail, with a copy to an applicant-provided email account permitted by agreement between the landlord or agent and applicant. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an owner of residential rental property or their agent does not perform a personal reference check or does not obtain a consumer credit report, they must return to the applicant any screening fee amount not used for purposes authorized by this section. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.

If an applicant has paid an application screening fee, the owner of residential rental property or their agent must provide the applicant who is the report's subject a copy of the consumer credit report by personal delivery, mail or email within seven days after receiving it. Residential-use evidence: supplied assessor description “Apartment 5 to 14 Units”. This does not establish a primary residence or the absence of exemptions.
